measurement: G's CEILING, pre-registered before the run (理 10882)
source: experience/traj/base_v1_7b — 2,000 episodes, the run G's head is trained on
method: split the 2,000 episodes by the label of their ONE hypothesis. A controller that chose PERFECTLY at that single decision point would turn every episode into a productive-labelled one, so the productive group's numbers are the arithmetic ceiling on G.

THE_CEILING.success: 68.0% — up from 59.9% baseline. MAXIMUM HEADROOM +8.1 points.
THE_CEILING.mean_actions: 6.15 — down from 6.85. MAXIMUM SAVING 0.70 actions, i.e. -10.2%.

AND_THE_TARGET_IS_ABOVE_THE_CEILING.target: 理's pre-registered objective for G: mean actions <= 5.6, a -15% cut
AND_THE_TARGET_IS_ABOVE_THE_CEILING.verdict: THE -15% TARGET IS UNREACHABLE. A PERFECT controller on this harness lands at 6.15 actions; 5.6 is below what choosing correctly every single time can buy. The target was set before anyone had computed what the choice is worth, and this join is why 理 asked for the ceiling BEFORE the run rather than after.
AND_THE_TARGET_IS_ABOVE_THE_CEILING.what_should_replace_it: either the objective moves to <= 6.15 (the ceiling) with G judged on the FRACTION of available headroom it captures, or the -15% stands and G is scored against an impossible bar. That is 理's to rule; I am not moving a pre-registered target on my own reading.

what_this_does_to_the_success_criterion.epsilon: ε = 2.5 points on every slice (>= 60.0% vs 62.5%) is a CAPABILITY-HELD criterion and is unaffected — it asks G not to LOSE, and the ceiling says it could gain up to 8.1.
what_this_does_to_the_success_criterion.reading: so the acceptance test is coherent on capability and incoherent on cost. Only the actions objective needs the ruling.

the_asymmetry_worth_stating: the wasted group's success rate is ZERO — 0 of 239. Not low: zero. An episode whose single hypothesis misses the bug region NEVER recovers, because the loop never re-hypothesises. That is the same fact as '9,668 of 13,696 steps are patch attempts', measured from the outcome side, and it is what makes the one decision worth a controller at all.
bounds: The ceiling assumes a perfect chooser AND that choosing correctly makes an episode behave like one that chose correctly on its own. A hard task that the base model localises by luck is not made easy by a controller localising it deliberately.
One run, 2,000 episodes, the 7B. The ceiling is specific to this harness and budget.
